/- SamplingOptimisationGeometryBench public-dev reference.
   Reuses the existing project proof; retain LICENSE and NOTICE. -/
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Geometry.LogConcavity
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Strong

open Set

example
    {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    {V : E → ℝ} {k : ℝ} (hV : StrongConvexOn (Set.univ : Set E) k V)
    (x₀ : E) (hx₀ : IsMinOn V (Set.univ : Set E) x₀) :
    ∀ x : E, V x₀ + (k / 4) * ‖x - x₀‖ ^ 2 ≤ V x := by
  intro x
  have hx₀_min : ∀ y : E, V x₀ ≤ V y := isMinOn_univ_iff.mp hx₀
  have hmid_min : V x₀ ≤ V ((1 / 2 : ℝ) • x₀ + (1 / 2 : ℝ) • x) := hx₀_min _
  have hstrong :=
    hV.2 (by simp : x₀ ∈ (Set.univ : Set E)) (by simp : x ∈ (Set.univ : Set E))
      (by norm_num : 0 ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) (by norm_num : 0 ≤ (1 / 2 : ℝ))
      (by norm_num : (1 / 2 : ℝ) + (1 / 2 : ℝ) = 1)
  have hstrong' :
      V ((1 / 2 : ℝ) • x₀ + (1 / 2 : ℝ) • x) ≤
        (1 / 2 : ℝ) * V x₀ + (1 / 2 : ℝ) * V x - (k / 8) * ‖x - x₀‖ ^ 2 := by
    rw [norm_sub_rev x₀ x] at hstrong
    convert hstrong using 1
    · simp [smul_eq_mul]
      ring_nf
  have hle := hmid_min.trans hstrong'
  nlinarith

Uses the exposed global minimizer at the midpoint.

before.source_note: Original exercise over the existing Samplinglib midpoint lemma. It is not presented as a verbatim textbook statement.
steps: At \(m=(x_0+x)/2\), strong convexity gives \[V(m)\le\tfrac12V(x_0)+\tfrac12V(x)-\tfrac k8\|x-x_0\|^2.\] The factor \(k/8\) comes from \((k/2)(1/2)(1/2)\).
Global minimality gives \(V(x_0)\le V(m)\). Combine the two inequalities and multiply by 2 to obtain \(V(x_0)+\tfrac k4\|x-x_0\|^2\le V(x)\). No derivative or limit was used.
This midpoint calculation proves the k/4 envelope, not the sharper k/2 constant. Obtaining a sharper result needs another argument; it must not be credited to this calculation.

The envelope alone is not a normalization theorem. A Gibbs-integrability consumer additionally needs an appropriate finite-dimensional reference measure, measurability, a positive confining modulus, and a Gaussian-integrability argument; positivity of the normalizer is a separate obligation. Here k need not even be positive.
